text:
"Do I really need a Google Business Profile if people can find my website?"

Yes.

Search "plumber near me" on your phone. The map and its listings usually sit above the websites.

No profile, no spot on the map.

It's free. I'd set it up this week.

Google's best trick for a local business is timing.

Someone's hot water system dies at 6am. They grab their phone and search.

That's the moment they're most ready to buy.

Show up right then, on the map or in the ads, and you're the one they call.

I've seen a busy Fremantle café disappear from Google Maps for weeks after its profile got suspended.

Same food.
Same coffee.
Same loyal locals.

The people searching "cafe near me" on a Saturday morning just couldn't find them.

Keep your profile clean.

A great website with no Google Business Profile is like a nice shop on a back street with no sign out the front.

A rough website with a solid profile still gets calls.

If I had to fix one first for a local tradie, it's the profile. Then the website.

How Google gets you clients, in two parts:

1. Be there when they search. Maps, results, ads.
2. Keep showing up until they're ready. Most people don't buy the first time.

Do one without the other and customers leak out the side.

Which part are you missing?

Quick check if you run Google Ads:

Assets > filter by Promotion.

Anything with "Google AI" in the Added by column is an offer Google wrote for you, pulled from your website.

Read every one. Would you honour it on the phone tomorrow?
